data.title: Ethereum price risks crashing to $1,500 as ETF outflows mount
data.description:
Ethereum (ETH) faces the possibility of another significant decline as persistent institutional withdrawals, weakening technical indicators, and growing macroeconomic uncertainty continue to pressure the cryptocurrency.

The second-largest cryptocurrency recently broke below the important $1,850 support level, increasing concerns that its correction could extend toward $1,500 in the coming weeks.

The current price action suggests that the broader bearish trend remains intact, although deeply oversold conditions could trigger a temporary recovery before another decline.

The outlook comes as US spot Ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have experienced seven consecutive weeks of net withdrawals totaling approximately $2.4 billion.

Ethereum ETF outflows continue despite consolidating price action

Institutional sentiment toward Ethereum has deteriorated considerably in recent weeks. US spot Ethereum ETFs have recorded seven consecutive weeks of net outflows, with approximately $2.4 billion withdrawn during that period.

The withdrawal continued this week, with $54.5 million redeemed by institutional investors from Monday to Wednesday. 

The sustained withdrawals suggest that investors are reducing exposure to ETH amid heightened market uncertainty.

Persistent inflationary pressure, rising energy prices, and uncertainty surrounding the conflict involving Iran are major factors contributing to the weaker investment environment.

These developments have complicated expectations for US monetary policy, with investors increasingly concerned about the possibility of tighter financial conditions.

Ethereum price outlook: ETH stays below $1,800 as analysts target $1,500

Ethereum's decline below $1,800 represents an important technical development. The level previously served as a significant accumulation area during August, when buyers helped support a strong recovery.

However, the latest breakdown suggests that the region has failed to hold as support. If the bearish trend persists, Ethereum could extend its decline towards the $1,500 psychological level. 

This level corresponds with an important historical support region that helped stabilize Ethereum during previous corrections.

A decline toward $1,500 would also bring ETH closer to the lows recorded in June 2026. The selling pressure could intensify if trading volumes remain weak and buyers fail to return.

Under that scenario, Ethereum could extend its decline toward $1,400, revisiting the price region last seen during its April 2025 bearish trend.

Despite the negative technical outlook, Ethereum's momentum indicators suggest that the recent decline may be becoming overstretched.

The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) has fallen into deeply oversold territory for the first time since June. The RSI currently reads 26, within the oversold region.  Historically, similar readings have preceded notable recoveries in Ethereum's price.

This could see Ethereum experience a relief rally in the short term, with the first potential recovery target standing near $1,900.

A sustained move above this level could allow ETH to challenge higher resistance, potentially extending toward $2,400.

However, the recovery could be temporary if broader market conditions remain unfavorable. Under its bearish scenario, Ethereum could rebound before eventually resuming its decline toward $1,500.

Could Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade support a recovery?

Ethereum's upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade represents another development that could influence its longer-term outlook.

The network's developers are preparing the upgrade for the final quarter of 2026, following earlier improvements introduced through the Pectra upgrade.

Although network upgrades can improve blockchain functionality and strengthen Ethereum's long-term competitiveness, their effect on token prices is not always immediate.

Nevertheless, continued development remains important for Ethereum's long-term position in the cryptocurrency industry.

data.title: Soybean price analysis: Brent oil price bounces off crucial support
data.description:
Soybean price is trading within a rather tight range as investors weigh the energy market and the overall supply/demand dynamics. The bulls attempts of a breakout late last week were unsuccessful as the differing factors failed to attract enough buyers. In the short term, sideways trading may continue, with a breakout being dependent on crucial resistance levels. 

Soybean price trades sideways amid a volatile energy market

CBOT soybean price has been trading sideways in recent sessions after easing from the bullish WASDE report. USDA’s forecast for the 2026/27 season included increased exports and lower ending stocks. This is despite the predicted surge in US production by 12 million bushels. US soybean exports are expected to increase by 25 million bushels while the global ending stocks have been lessened by 0.8 million tons. 

According to the latest NASS crop progress report, soybean harvesting is 96% complete across the United States. This is slightly higher than the average pace of 95%. 

At the same time, the Export Inspections data indicate that soybean shipments for the week that ended on 12th November were 1.708 million metric tonnes (MMT). This was a decline of 10.8% from the previous week, but an increase of 41.7% from a similar period in 2025. Notably, China was the leading destination with a shipment of 691,670 MT. Increased US exports and brisk Chinese demand continue to support soybean prices. 

However, a stronger US dollar and weaker Brazilian Real are curbing the asset’s price gains. Earlier on Tuesday, the  Brazilian Real extended its losses to a fresh 19-month low before easing slightly. Over the past three weeks, the South American currency has plunged by close to 15%, enticing local producers to increase export volumes for more US dollars. At the same time, a stronger greenback renders the dollar-priced asset more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies. 

In the ensuing sessions, investors within the soybean market will also be eyeing crude oil prices. The crude oil market has been rather volatile in recent sessions amid conflicting drivers. On the one hand, the persistent conflicts in the Middle East are offering steady support to energy prices. However, investors are increasingly betting on a global supply glut. Crude oil prices largely impact the demand for biofuel. In addition to corn and sugarcane, soybean is a major source of biofuel.  

Soybean price technical analysis

CBOT soybean futures made subtle movements on Tuessday as the agricultural commodity continues to trade sideways. Late last week, the bulls attempted a breakout, surging to a one-and-a-half week high at $12.41 a bushel before easing back to its tight trading range. At the time of writing, soybean price was at $12.29, up by 0.04%.  

A look at its daily chart points to continued sideways trading in the short term, as investors eye the driving fundamentals and technical indicators. To begin with, CBOT soybean price remains below the short-term 25-day EMA and the medium-term 50-day EMA. Indeed, in late October, the two technical indicators formed a bearish death-cross pattern that is still in place. The bearish formation occurs when short-term MA crosses the medium/long-term MA to the downside as an indication of further losses. Besides, its RSI of 46 supports the thesis on curbed gains and range-bound trading. 

Even with these bearish technical indicators, soybean price continues to trade above the long-term 200-day EMA. This is an indication that the long-term support is still intact.  

In line with these technical indicators, and the fundamentals, the range between the support level of $12.14 and the resistance along the 25-day EMA at $12.35 is worth watching. Further gains will likely be curbed at $12.41. On the flip side, additional losses will invalidate this cautious thesis as the sellers eye the lower support level at $12.09.

data.title: SpaceX stock rises as Citi sees wireless network and AI growth potential
data.description:
SpaceX shares SPCX gained around 1.7% on Wednesday as investors assessed the company's expanding wireless ambitions, plans for artificial intelligence infrastructure in Texas and continued launch activity.

The stock also received support from positive analyst commentary.

Morgan Stanley reiterated its Overweight rating, suggesting investors consider buying shares during periods of weakness.

The brokerage said SpaceX had shown resilience despite volatility in AI-related stocks and could become a more durable holding as the market's AI investment theme evolves.

Meanwhile, Citi maintained its $280 price target on SpaceX, implying approximately 92% upside from current levels, as it examined the company's potential entry into the US mobile network market.

Citi sees SpaceX building its own mobile network

Citi believes SpaceX may need to develop a substantial ground-based network if it wants to compete with established US wireless operators, even as it plans to use Starlink satellites to reduce its reliance on traditional telecommunications infrastructure.

The brokerage highlighted comments from SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen at the TomorrowX Summit, where he outlined the company's plans for a wireless network that would rely less heavily on conventional cell towers.

SpaceX believes Starlink satellites could carry network traffic through space rather than depending as heavily on traditional fibre connections.

This could allow the company to operate a more efficient network using smaller cell sites.

However, Citi said a substantial number of macro cell sites would still be necessary, particularly in urban and suburban areas.

Ground infrastructure would help provide reliable indoor coverage and sufficient network capacity.

SpaceX could build its own network, acquire an existing telecommunications operator or operate as a mobile virtual network operator using another company's infrastructure.

Citi considers building its own network the most likely option.

Last month, SpaceX agreed to acquire Grain Management's nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz wireless spectrum licences, covering up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum.

The acquisition could strengthen Starlink Mobile's coverage, particularly indoors and in areas with weaker cellular signals.

JPMorgan had also highlighted the need for SpaceX to develop ground-based infrastructure to compete with established US telecom operators.

Texas approves SpaceX data centre and power project

SpaceX shares also gained after Texas resumed permitting for artificial intelligence facilities and approved the company's proposed data centre and natural-gas power plant, according to Politico.

The $24 billion project is located in the Rio Grande Valley, where SpaceX is headquartered.

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality issued a permit allowing the company to install 35 natural-gas-powered turbines.

The facility is expected to generate 750 megawatts of electricity.

It will not be connected to the state's electrical grid, and the permit allows it to emit up to 248 tons of nitrogen oxides annually.

The approval follows a September order by outgoing Texas Governor Greg Abbott to pause approvals for such projects.

Abbott lost his re-election bid earlier this month to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who won the election to become the state's next governor.

Upcoming Falcon 9 launch

SpaceX is also targeting Thursday, November 19, for a Falcon 9 launch of the USSF-317 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

The four-hour launch window is scheduled to open at 6:46 p.m. Pacific time, or 9:46 p.m. Eastern. A backup opportunity is available on Friday, November 20, at 8:26 p.m. Pacific time.

The first-stage booster is scheduled to make its 11th flight, following previous launches including NROL-105, USSF-385 and eight Starlink missions.

SpaceX plans to land the booster on its Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean.

data.title: Why is Nvidia stock falling over 2% on Wednesday?
data.description:
Nvidia shares NVDA fell 2.2% on Wednesday, extending their decline to a fifth consecutive session, as the US House Committee on Energy and Commerce demanded a formal briefing from the chipmaker over alleged export control violations and former CEO Jensen Huang's reported links to a suspected Chinese spy.

Representative Brett Guthrie, chairman of the committee, sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress requesting that company officials appear before lawmakers no later than December 2.

The inquiry focuses on whether Nvidia circumvented federal restrictions intended to prevent advanced artificial intelligence technology from reaching China.

Lawmakers are also examining allegations that a senior company official attempted to interfere with a federal investigation.

The developments add to the pressure on Nvidia as it navigates a leadership transition and scrutiny over national security concerns, despite strong quarterly results and an upbeat revenue outlook.

Congressional probe focuses on export control allegations

In his letter, Guthrie said the reported events raised questions about Nvidia's compliance with federal export laws and the effectiveness of its security controls.

The congressional investigation centres on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer suspected of helping Chinese companies circumvent US export restrictions.

On November 16, the Justice Department and Commerce Department publicly confirmed a joint criminal investigation into the company.

Reports have also linked Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is alleged to have a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, to suspected Chinese intelligence activities.

According to Guthrie's letter, investigators are examining claims that she established a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia hardware.

Lawmakers are also looking into allegations that the Commerce Department transferred its initial investigation into Megaspeed to the Justice Department last year after Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce officials seeking information about the inquiry.

These allegations have not been established as findings of wrongdoing by Nvidia.

Leadership transition adds to investor concerns

The controversy has coincided with significant changes at Nvidia's senior leadership level.

On November 8, Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in an internal email to employees and said the company's board had launched an independent investigation into national security concerns raised by media reports.

Four days later, he announced his departure from company leadership.

Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, took over as interim CEO while the company works with an external firm to find a permanent replacement.

The uncertainty has weighed on investor sentiment, with Nvidia shares declining for five consecutive trading sessions and facing the prospect of a seventh consecutive weekly loss.

However, Wall Street analysts have pointed to the company's latest financial results as evidence that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.

Nvidia reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share, beating analyst expectations by 21 cents.

Revenue reached $115.84 billion, up 103.2% from a year earlier and $7.13 billion above forecasts.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, compared with analyst estimates of $124.89 billion.

The forecast assumes no data centre computing revenue from China.

Analysts remain positive on Nvidia's outlook

Several Wall Street firms have maintained positive views on Nvidia despite the leadership uncertainty.

RBC reiterated its Outperform rating, citing demand that continues to exceed supply, a product roadmap extending over the next three years and limited near-term competitive risks due to industry supply constraints.

The firm also highlighted rising supply purchase commitments as evidence of strong demand visibility.

Morgan Stanley maintained its Overweight rating, pointing to strong demand for AI computing and Nvidia's competitive position.

Its analysts also viewed the company's willingness to provide forward-looking commentary as a positive.

Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275 while retaining an Outperform rating.

The firm said Nvidia's near- and medium-term demand outlook remained unchanged despite Huang's departure.

The company also has $227.3 billion remaining under its share buyback authorisation.

Kress described returning capital to shareholders as a top priority during the earnings call and said Nvidia could fully utilise the remaining authorisation by fiscal 2028.

Jefferies said the buyback programme offered another potential source of support for the stock, while noting that investors still need greater visibility into the company's strategic direction following the leadership transition.

Meanwhile, Kress said Nvidia was raising its fiscal 2028 outlook and expected revenue growth of approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously and on a higher fiscal 2027 base.

data.title: Cathie Wood was right on the money about these 2 stocks
data.description:
Every new artificial intelligence (AI) data center needs chips.

The AI agents running on those chips need to fetch data, call software tools, and interact with websites.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Investment Management found winners on both sides of that buildout.

AMD and Cloudflare have seen explosive rallies since the famed investor first gained exposure to both.

They are proving a perfect example of how AI demand is spreading from the companies that supply the hardware to those that keep the applications running.

AMD turned a server-chip foothold into an AI business

ARK first bought about 640,000 AMD shares in the third quarter of 2018. At the time, they were going for about $31 only.

The firm later exited its position in Advanced Micro Devices, only to reestablish it in early 2023, at roughly $98 each.

As of writing, those same shares are trading at about $507 – suggesting Cathie Wood has secured a more than 5x gain on AMD.

The business behind that massive rally sells two kinds of chips into the same data center.

EPYC server processors handle general computing, while Instinct accelerators do the heavy lifting for AI models.

Demand for both pushed Q3 data center revenue up 97% to $8.5 billion.

The division’s operating profit climbed to $2.9 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier – showing how much of the sales growth is reaching the bottom line.

CEO Lisa Su expects data center chips to account for about 80% of AMD’s revenue in 2027.

That gives AMD more to gain as cloud companies expand capacity and more exposure if they slow the pace of new deployments.

Cloudflare found a way to turn developer adoption into revenue

Cloudflare first appeared in ARK’s reported holdings in the fourth quarter of 2020, when the stock traded at roughly $76.

In comparison, it’s now going for roughly $285, representing about 3.75x return on Cathie Wood’s initial investment.

The company now gives developers a place to run applications and AI agents through Workers – expanding what it can sell to businesses that already depend on its network for both security and performance.

Cloudflare passed 10 million active developers and added a record 158,000 paying customers in its fiscal Q3.

Revenue soared 39% to $782.5 million, and dollar-based net retention reached 122%.

That means the same group of customers generated 22% more revenue over a year after accounting for customers that cut spending or left.

Management also expects GAAP profitability in the fourth quarter, ahead of its earlier target of reaching that milestone by 2028.

The margin story helps explain why.

Workers carries a lower gross margin than some Cloudflare products, but it costs less to sell.

That gives Cloudflare a path to higher operating margins as developers turn experiments into applications they pay to run.

data.title: XRP bulls are losing control: could the price crash below $0.90?
data.description:
XRP continues to struggle on Thursday as persistent selling pressure and weakening derivatives activity raise concerns about further losses.

The cryptocurrency is showing signs of bearish positioning in its futures markets, while on-chain indicators suggest that large investors remain cautious.

According to CoinGlass, funding rates for XRP and XLM have turned negative, indicating that traders holding short positions are paying those holding long positions.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant data shows sell-side dominance across the spot and futures markets of both cryptocurrencies, suggesting that buying demand remains insufficient to reverse the prevailing weakness.

XRP funding rates turn negative as bearish sentiment persists

Derivatives market indicators suggest that traders remain cautious about the near-term outlook for XRP. According to CoinGlass, XRP's funding rate stood at -0.0068% on Thursday. 

Funding rates are periodic payments exchanged between traders holding long and short positions in perpetual futures contracts.

When funding rates are negative, traders holding short positions generally pay those holding long positions. This typically indicates that bearish positioning is more prominent in the perpetual futures market.

Additional derivatives indicators reveal differences in positioning between XRP and Stellar traders. According to CoinGlass, XRP's long-to-short ratio stood at 0.93 on Thursday, approaching its lowest level in more than a month.

A reading below 1 indicates that short positions outnumber long positions under the metric's methodology. This suggests that bearish traders currently have the advantage in XRP's derivatives market.

On-chain and trading activity indicators reinforce the cautious outlook for XRP and Stellar.

According to CryptoQuant, XRP's spot and futures markets are experiencing sell-side dominance, indicating that aggressive selling activity continues to outweigh buying demand.

The broader picture suggests that XRP remains vulnerable to further weakness unless demand improves.

XRP remains below $1 as major moving averages signal weakness

XRP's technical outlook remains bearish as the cryptocurrency struggles to recover above important resistance levels.

The token trades around $0.98 on Thursday, remaining below its major daily Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

The 50-day EMA stands near $1.198, while the 100-day EMA is positioned around $1.250. Meanwhile, the 200-day EMA sits at approximately $1.324.

These moving averages form several layers of resistance above the current market price. Trading below all three indicators also means that recovery attempts could encounter selling pressure as prices approach previously important technical levels.

The psychological $1 level represents the first major obstacle. A sustained recovery above this threshold could improve short-term sentiment, but it would not necessarily confirm a broader bullish reversal.

XRP's momentum indicators suggest that the recent decline may be losing some intensity. The daily Relative Strength Index stands near 26, placing the cryptocurrency close to, or just inside, oversold territory.

Meanwhile, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence indicator remains negative, suggesting that bearish momentum continues to dominate.

Nevertheless, the indicator shows signs of moderating downside momentum. This suggests that selling pressure may be easing, potentially allowing XRP to stage a temporary rebound.

XRP faces several important resistance levels as it attempts to recover from its recent decline. The first major barrier stands at the psychological $1 level.

A sustained breakout above this threshold could encourage buyers to target the next horizontal resistance near $1.160. Beyond this level, the 50-day EMA at $1.198 represents another significant obstacle.

A recovery above the 50-day EMA could provide an early indication that short-term bearish momentum is weakening.

However, XRP would still face resistance at the 100-day EMA near $1.250 and the horizontal barrier around $1.300. Further resistance stands at the 200-day EMA near $1.324.

Reclaiming this longer-term moving average would provide stronger evidence of an improving technical structure.

If buying momentum strengthens significantly, additional resistance levels could emerge near $1.540 and $1.900.

On the downside, the weekend low of $0.8925 remains a key support level. Failure to defend this support could see XRP extend its losses towards the $0.80 demand zone. 

For now, XRP's near-term outlook remains bearish while the cryptocurrency trades below $1 and its major daily moving averages.

data.title: Anthropic’s $81 billion IPO eclipses SpaceX, but can its valuation hold?
data.description:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, raising $81.34 billion ahead of its Nasdaq debut and overtaking SpaceX’s original share sale.

The Claude developer expanded its offering to 980 million shares and priced above the indicated $70–$78 range, valuing the company at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The deal underscores investors’ appetite for artificial intelligence, even as questions grow about whether the industry’s huge computing bills will translate into lasting profits.

Anthropic’s shares are expected to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker ANT. Investors will now judge whether extraordinary revenue growth can support one of the richest valuations ever assigned to a newly listed company.

Anthropic tops SpaceX’s original IPO, but with a catch

Anthropic increased its offering from 825 million shares to 980 million as demand intensified. The company is selling about 956.35 million shares, with existing shareholders holding the rest.

At $83 apiece, the total sale is worth $81.34 billion. Around $79.38 billion of that represents shares issued by Anthropic, rather than proceeds going to selling investors.

The offering exceeds the $75 billion SpaceX initially raised in June.

However, Elon Musk’s rocket company ultimately collected approximately $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their option to buy additional shares. Anthropic has not yet surpassed that enlarged amount.

A separate $26 billion private placement involving major technology companies could lift Anthropic’s combined equity fundraising above $107 billion, subject to closing. That private transaction is distinct from the IPO itself.

The scale reflects the appeal of owning a direct stake in frontier AI development, an opportunity largely unavailable to ordinary stock-market investors.

Anthropic IPO: Revenue is soaring, but so are computing commitments

Anthropic’s annualised revenue run rate reached $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion in a single month. That is an annualised pace, not revenue already booked over a year.

Actual sales for the first nine months of 2026 reached $33.24 billion, up more than twelvefold from a year earlier. But computing and infrastructure expenses consumed approximately 57% of that revenue.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of about $1.26 billion for the period. Its much larger accounting net loss was heavily affected by non-cash adjustments to financial liabilities, rather than representing equivalent cash spent.

More daunting are roughly $900.9 billion of purchase and lease commitments, principally for computing infrastructure, stretching into 2045. They are multiyear obligations, not bills payable immediately.

Phil Blancato, Osaic’s chief market strategist, told Business Insider that “there’s still room for the business to grow well beyond where it is today”, pointing to AI’s potential across knowledge work.

Anthropic IPO valuation: Can $1.5 trillion valuation survive debut?

At the offering price, Anthropic is valued at roughly 18.5 times its latest annualised revenue run rate. That leaves shareholders dependent on continued expansion and improving margins.

“Great companies, great technology, but are they going to be able to convert this into big profits?” University of Florida IPO researcher Jay Ritter asked in comments to TheStreet.

Competition from OpenAI, Google and cheaper AI models could limit how much Anthropic charges customers, even if adoption keeps growing.

Some professional investors prefer to wait. “We wouldn’t be a buyer at this level,” Strategy Asset Managers chief executive Tom Hulick told Reuters, saying his firm would look for declines after the debut.

Strong initial demand may support the shares, but Anthropic’s first public earnings and any insider selling could test that enthusiasm.

data.title: Gold price falls as Fed hike odds jump and GLD, IAU ETF outflows surge
data.description:
Gold price remained under pressure on Thursday as investors bet that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next meeting. The metal traded at $3,728, about $32 above this week’s low of $3,696. It remains well below its all-time high of $5,600, and technical indicators suggest further downside in the near term.

Gold price has slumped amid Fed rate hike odds

Gold has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months as demand among investors waned. ETF Database data shows that the SPDR Gold ETF (GLD) has had over $1.37 billion in outflows in the last 30 days. The iShares Gold Trust (IAU) has shed over $279 million in assets in the same period. 

Investors are concerned about the rising probability that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates in the coming meeting. The bank has already hiked rates by 25 basis points, and there is a consensus that it will hike in the coming meeting. Odds of the hike happening have jumped to over 99% on Polymarket. 

Minutes released on Wednesday showed that Federal Reserve officials struck a hawkish tone at their last meeting, even though they held interest rates steady. Rather than raise rates, they chose to pause while they gather more information on inflation and the economy.

Recent numbers have confirmed their view that inflation is still stubbornly high. The most recent data showed that the headline and core Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% and 0.3%, respectively. Inflation has remained above the 2% target in the last five years, and this trend may continue as President Donald Trump considers launching fresh attacks against Iran.

Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data showed that the labor market remained strong last month. The most recent data showed that the American economy created over 165k jobs as the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%. Retail sales remained resilient last month.

Gold has also dropped amid elevated bond yields. The ten-year yield crossed the important resistance level of 5% and has remained above it in the past few weeks. Short-term yields have also continued rising, making gold less attractive. 

Central banks are buying gold

On the positive side, central banks have continued to accumulate gold this year. The most active ones are from China, Uzbekistan, and Poland. In total, central banks have bought 170 tons of gold, which are currently worth about $21 billion. The real figure is much higher than that since many countries don’t provide the most accurate data.

Gold may also benefit from the rising US debt, which has jumped to over $40.6 trillion, a few months after it crossed the crucial $40 trillion milestone. The metal is widely seen as a good hedge against the rising spending by US authorities.

Gold price technical analysis

Gold chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that gold has been in a strong downward trend in the past few months. Most recently, it dropped from a high of $4,695 in August to the current $3,737.

Gold has slumped below the important support level of $3,946, its lowest level on June 30th. It has remained below the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has continued falling.

Therefore, gold will likely continue falling in the near term, with the next psychological level to watch will be at $3,500. On the flip side, a move above the resistance level of $3,946 will invalidate the bearish outlook and point to more gains. The next key catalysts for gold will be the nonfarm payrolls, inflation, and the December Federal Reserve interest rate decision.

data.title: Samsung and SK Hynix stocks fall again as Nvidia earnings boost fades
data.description:
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix stocks fell on Thursday, reversing part of their previous session's gains as Nvidia's record earnings failed to restore lasting confidence in the artificial intelligence trade.

Samsung declined 2.4% and SK Hynix lost 1.3% by 11:20 am in Seoul. The benchmark KOSPI slipped 0.94% to 5,019.72, having briefly traded below 5,000.

The weakness followed a 2.89% decline in Nvidia's US shares on Wednesday, despite the chipmaker reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly sales and an upbeat forecast.

Nvidia earnings impact: Rally quickly loses momentum

Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion on Tuesday, an increase of 103% from a year earlier. Its data-centre division generated $107.6 billion, while management projected about $130 billion in sales for the following quarter.

The figures reinforced expectations of sustained spending on AI infrastructure and initially lifted South Korean semiconductor shares.

On Wednesday, Samsung rose 2.31% to 194,700 won and SK Hynix gained 4.19% to 1,144,000 won. The KOSPI advanced 1.99%, recovering from its previous close below 5,000.

But Nvidia's decline during the subsequent US session suggested investors were reluctant to treat one strong earnings report as proof that AI investments will deliver attractive returns.

Neil Shah, vice-president of research at Counterpoint, told Reuters the results had stabilised sentiment but “postponed rather than permanently cured investor anxiety”.

Concerns over data-centre financing, export restrictions and Nvidia's management transition following Jensen Huang's resignation continue to cloud the outlook.

Foreign selling adds pressure to South Korea semiconductor stocks

Investors outside South Korea were net sellers of 216.55 billion won in KOSPI shares by 11:20 am Thursday. Institutions sold another 159.27 billion won, while retail investors bought 278.79 billion won.

The outflows help explain why shares have struggled to hold gains despite impressive semiconductor earnings and resilient demand for memory chips.

Samsung and SK Hynix have benefited from elevated prices for high-bandwidth memory and server DRAM.

But buyers of their shares are increasingly looking beyond current orders to ask how long those margins can endure.

More production capacity, delayed data-centre construction or weaker cloud spending could eventually bring tighter competition and lower pricing power.

Jung Hee-chan of Samsung Futures told Money Today that technology companies should lead Korean earnings growth next year, although investors need greater confidence that profits can be sustained before rewarding the sector with higher valuations.

Samsung, SK Hynix stocks: Is semiconductor sell-off becoming excessive?

US monetary policy is adding another challenge. Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting, released Wednesday, showed that almost all officials expected further interest-rate increases would be appropriate under their baseline outlooks.

Higher yields can make future earnings less valuable in today's terms, weighing heavily on technology companies priced for years of growth.

Thursday's planned Nasdaq debut of AI developer Anthropic is another test of investor appetite for expensive technology businesses.

Still, not every analyst sees the downturn as justified.

Kiwoom Securities analyst Han Ji-young told Seoul Economic Daily that South Korean share prices already reflect much of the foreseeable economic and AI-related uncertainty.

A less negative market response and improving foreign flows could therefore support a rebound.

data.title: Lenovo Group stock analysis after earnings: is this Dell rival a buy or sell?
data.description:
Lenovo Group stock remained under pressure on Thursday after the technology company published its financial results. It was trading at H$16.72, down by over 55% from its all-time high. Its technicals suggest that it has more downside in the near term. 

Lenovo Group’s business continued doing well

Lenovo Group, a leading competitor to Dell and HP Enterprise, reported strong financial results for the latest quarter. The figures show the company’s business continued to grow, driven by ongoing investment in artificial intelligence (AI).

The results showed that its revenue growth gained momentum. Its revenue soared by 46% YoY to $30.2 billion, with its AI related figure rising by 79. 

A look at its segments shows the business is thriving. The Intelligent Devices Group generated more than $17.4 billion in revenue, up 17% year on year, with an operating margin of 7.1%. This growth came as the company prioritized higher-priced devices, even as the number of units sold fell. 

Indeed, its premium PCs contributed to 63% of all PC shippings during the quarter. Recent data by Gartner showed that its PC sales dropped by 22.4% to 14.9 million during the quarter. Its PC margins have also dropped because of the ongoing memory shortage.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group’s revenue surged 178%, and its AI server pipeline reached $54 billion. 

Lenovo’s AI business is being driven by American hyperscalers, neoclouds, and Asian data center companies. Some of the revenue is coming from Asian data centers, especially in places like China and Malaysia. Lenovo’s Solutions and Services Group (SSG) grew by 205 to $3.1 billion. 

Still, the company made a $713 million loss during the quarter after losing over $1.19 billion in the same period last year. The loss was driven by fair value loss of $3.9 billion on derivative financial liabilities. 

Concerns about AI growth remains

Lenovo Group and other competitors have dropped in the past few months. For example, Dell stock has plunged by 46% from its highest point this year. It has dropped to its lowest level since May 28 this year.

HP Enterprise has also dropped to $45.78, down by 37% from the year-to-date high, while Super Micro Computer (SMCI) dropped by 52% in this period. Other companies in the AI space like Micron, SanDisk, and Western Digital have all plunged.

Investors are concerned about the potential slowdown in the coming months that would impact demand for its products. 

On the positive side, there are signs that demand is continuing growing. For example, Nvidia’s earnings report showed that its revenue jumped to $115 billion in the third quarter, much higher than the expected $108 billion. 

Lenovo Group stock technical analysis

Lenovo Group stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Lenovo Group’s stock has continued its strong sell-off in the past few months. It has slumped from $37 in September to the current $16.7. This retreat coincided with the ongoing weakness of other top companies in the AI space.

The stock has dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level of $19.73. In most cases, moving below that retracement normally confirms a bearish breakout. 

The stock has dropped below the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA) and the two lines are about to cross each other. A crossover would lead to a death cross, a popular bearish outlook.

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of $14.78, the 78.6% retracement level. A move below that level will point to more losses towards $10. In the future, however, there is a likelihood that the stock will bounce back, potentially to $20 and above.
